title: Perfect app
text: Routinery is a brilliant app for anyone who wants to get their day on track and stick to good habits. You set up routines like your morning or evening schedule, add tasks, and decide how long each one should take. The app then guides you step by step, making it easy to stay on top of things. It’s simple, clean, and super flexible, though I wish it had an option for tasks without timers—sometimes you just need a checklist, like for taking meds, without the countdown. Still, if you’re looking for structure and flow in your day, this app is a total win!

title: Pomodoro but way better.
text: If you like pomodoro, but it feels artificial or like the focus blocks can last for too much or too little time, this is perfect for you. I’ve always stepped up my game under the pressure of a timer, but very little of what I do can be accomplished in exactly 25 minutes. This allows me to set a time goal appropriate to the task. Check e-mails - 18 minutes; check in with team - 30 minutes; break - 8 minutes; research - 45 minutes, and so forth. I also love it as a tool to make sure all the essential cleaning gets done in a short session. It’s not as satisfying as fully finishing each cleaning task, but it makes sure all the key items get hit even if you only have a little time.

title: straight forward and easy to use
text:
i’ve developed these great routine blocks. I press play and it’s so easy for me to get through what I know I need to do. Instead of thinking about these giant list and all these things that I need to be consistent at I just press play and I get through them and it’s very customizable. You can’t have it switched on its own. You can manually do it. You can add time you can rearrange the order the day of you can also have it speak out certain things connect links if you’re a follow let’s say a YouTube warm-up video or there’s a form online that you need to use so I link certain websites for my workouts and I link certain YouTube videos for my daily stretches. 

The user interface of this program is simple, straightforward, clean and not distracting. It helps hold you accountable gives you nudges and helps you see where you have spent your time. I have ADHD and this has been a lifesaver to get things done. I’ve tried so many apps, but this simple straightforward and easy to use program is my favorite and has worked the best for me. Their free version is great and the paid version is very affordable at under five dollars a month. I definitely recommend for anyone trying to be more consistent in their life bringing in better routine routines, or struggle with ADHD.

title: Lifesaver for my ADHD
text:
I love this app. I have tried so many other habit tracker/to-do apps and none have come close to managing my adhd symptoms like this one does. A timed to-do list is great for managing time blindness and forgetfulness. It’s helping me to keep a strict routine that betters my health and makes life more manageable for me!! 

The best part is I can pair it with my Apple Watch so that I can put my phone down and not tempt myself to get distracted scrolling or online shopping. It also pairs well with my iPad, which I’ve set up on my desk so that I can physically see the pomodoro-style timer for work tasks!!

My suggestions: 

The AI suggestions for routine items are amazing. I wish that they would add more variety of work tasks to the mix though, and that the “suggested tasks” would be more specific to the tasks I’ve already added to the routine. Sometimes, the suggested tasks are already in the routine! 

I also wish that there was a feature where you could “unroll” the routines into one big, timed task list, where you can see everything that needs to be done for that day. 

 I’m a very visual person so the running list would be really cool and helpful! 

I also think it would be helpful if we could schedule individual tasks to show up in the running task list at various intervals (I.e weekly, bi-weekly, monthly). I don’t want to have to make a “bi-weekly cleaning routine”; I want those tasks to show up automatically on the days that I have to complete them.

I think that a running task list with the ability to schedule certain tasks to show up periodically would really help me and it would be an amazing feature to add to the app! :) 

Tl;dr: Overall, this app is seriously changing my life. I can’t tell you how helpful it is for me. I’ve recommended it to my therapist to share with her adhd patients as well!

title: Good app but could be better.
text:
I really like this app so far been using it for a couple days on a free trial and will probably subscribe to the yearly plan. However there are some things I would like to see changed or maybe I just haven’t figured it out yet. 

First the live activities on the iPhone doesn’t update once one task ends it doesn’t show the next task it just shows the first task with a “+hours”

Second I would like to be able to check off my activities once they are done. When an activity is done and it moves on to the next activity automatically you can’t go back to your Home Screen to check off the activities or create new activities your stuck on the screen with the timer. If you press the X  at the top it promos you to finish the activity. 

Third I would like to have routine  start by themselves. For example I have a routine that starts at 1:30am on Monday and ends at 1:30 am on Tuesday. Then I have another that starts at 1:30 am on tuesdays but I have to manually start the routine on Tuesday. There should be an auto start option to start the routine right away. 

I will keep updating this review cause I like this app. Maybe one day i can give it a 5 star.

title: Lifesaver
text:
Hi there! I’m a 15 year old, with ADD (another form of ADHD) and autism.
I always get distracted and lose track of time, which results in me having stressful mornings, never fully finishing my routine, and being late all the time.

However, this app just works some magic, I don’t know how to explain it. Before I found the app, I could use 4 hours on my mourning routine, and still not finish.
Now I can do everything within an hour.
The way that you can make your OWN routine, and quickly rearrange the order or add another task if you have a different day, is absolutely amazing.
I use the free version, and I have no complaints.

To whoever made this app, THANK YOU so so MUCH! I don’t think you understand what change this made to my life❤️

title: Life changing for my AuDHD
text: I started this app a few weeks ago when I accepted that, because of my autism, I’m not really able to form habits. That was liberating to realize and allowed me to embrace my rigid routines. However many of my rigid routines were keeping  me stuck. Routinery allowed me to create better routines and it’s helped me so much with time blindness and being able to have a more production morning. Otherwise I’m just stuck on YouTube. I also love that if I’m unable to complete my routine for a day or 2, it just doesn’t fall off like it used to. All I need to do is press play on the routines I created and I’m reminded exactly what my routine was. Frees up a lot of mental space. Highly recommended!

title: Helpful for ADHD
text: I have severe ADHD and haven’t had the best luck with medication, so I’m fully relying on coping skills and strategies to manage my symptoms. Initiating tasks, maintaining focus, and being aware of time passing are all things I struggle with a lot. And this app helps me with that. One of my routines is called “quick morning” for when I need to leave the house early, like for an 8am meeting. Watching the time tick down keeps me aware of how much time is passing, and how much time things are taking. Watching it tick down challenges me to be on time by racing the clock. I don’t need to panic trying to remember what to do because I’m following all of the necessary steps in order. And I’m less stressed about being late knowing that I’ll be ready at the end time of the routine. If you struggle with ADHD or any other time management or motivation issues, this is one of the few apps I’ve actually found helpful for more than like 3 days.

title: Best routine app on the apps store
text:
Pros:

It’s really amazing all around, it allows you to save routines, then set alarms and shortcuts to start them. The countdown for each step is really nice for someone with ADHD and keeps me on task. The UX is cute and clean. There is a huge list of cool icons to use to represent each step and the routine as a whole (though those icons are seemingly randomly assigned as you create each step and you need to go back and correct them)

Missing features:

Missing a few features that could make things a little easier. You can’t easily add routines by copying and pasting them from outside the app. I have many routines saved in my notes app and I need to retype each step into Routinery to add them. Not too big an issue but still frustrating (especially since I have ADHD). Also, I’d love to be able to quick edit routines when I’m done with them in order to tweak and adjust them for further use. (Like adjusting the time for each step, adding steps I forgot, etc.)

I’ve also seen other apps use AI to quickly generate steps of a routine for you as a starting point. This could be a good “pro” feature addition down the line.

Overall, this is an incredible app that has been making my life much easier. Seriously, thank you so much for making this 😊✅

text: I am probably the person who has tried every schedule, routine, and self care app in the App Store. I recently started using Routinery’s free version, and I feel like an entirely new person! The timer for each task really lets me plan my day down to the minute, and then stick to it! Because there’s room for error, the timer also helps me learn how long tasks take me, and will let me give myself enough time later! If I’ve overestimated how much time I need, then the routine gets done earlier! I’ve never been more productive in my LIFE and being without meds has always made things difficult. I have a streak of about three weeks and I feel so transformed… there is paid version option, but I don’t use it. It’s just become part of my morning ritual to set up my morning and afternoon routines! I love this app and 100% recommend it to anyone with motivation issues, you won’t burn out of this method, so give it a shot!!

title: No seriously, get this app.
text:
When I tell you that I have recommended this app to literally everyone in my life, I mean e v e r y o n e. 
Oh, you have ADHD so you have no idea how long it actually takes for you to take a shower? Good news, they planned for that. 
Oh, you have a super changing schedule and so a routine that’ll work for one day won’t work for another day? Good news, they planned for that too. 
Oh, you’re sick or on vacation or otherwise incapable of complaining routine and you need to rest? Good news, they also planned for that too! 
Seriously, just get the app. I’ve literally kept my streak up for almost 300 days because it’s so easy to change it and adapt or rest and not feel like a failure. Do you know how many things I’ve done consistently for almost 300 days straight? Maybe eat? Maybe? I’m paying real life human dollars for this app and it is worth every penny.

title: Great Habit Tracker but could improve
text:
This app is a great way to remember and track daily tasks and habits/routines that I don’t want to rewrite every day and clutter up my weekly planner.
Love: the timer voice that goes off to tell you it’s time for the next task or that minutes have passed etc., that you can either do the timer or check off the tasks on your own, the streak count & streak saver, the reflection page at the end of a routine timer, the aesthetics and simplicity, 
❗️Please Improve: -when you just check off the tasks instead of using the timer, there is no acknowledgement of completing that routine other than a check mark next to it in the list, there NEEDS to be a celebratory graphic when you check off the last task (maybe even a small one on every check to keep you encouraged as you go)! Otherwise it doesn’t feel like you even completed it, it’s not rewarding enough especially for ADHD. Please add some more 🎊🎉  rewarding graphics, it would massively increase my use and enjoyment of this app!

Considering that I’m AuDHD preferring routines but struggling to maintain it so I need a lot of encouragement and motivation. I like how this begins with a lot of inspiration and a lot to start me on & a lot of awesome daily routines and even therapeutic in coping with depression. Is there any way you can include more about depression and for anxiety? I battle with anxiety a lot. I like how it gives a timer, because I really don’t have any concept of time and I take forever with hyper focus or I get distracted so using a timer really helps. Thank you for this app. Also, I’m not too interested in the social part so kept mine on private. 🥰

title: Great app - frustrating sometimes though
text:
This is only way I’m able to start my day quickly. It’s a lifesaver! 

I’m struggling with it a bit lately though. I started a routine on my watch. I skipped some things, hoping they’d be added to the end—the watch doesn’t offer a choice of what to do when you skip like the phone does. 

After completing a couple of tasks, I needed to do the skipped tasks before moving on, but I couldn’t rearrange or do anything at all. Pretty normal for the watch app. I went to the phone app, and it says I have to end the watch routine and start it on the phone. I feel like they used to both run at the same time, which was really helpful. 

After ending the watch routine, I can’t unskip the skipped tasks on the phone. I can’t check them off either. They’re just.. crossed off for the day? I’m so confused as to why this is the way it’s working. If I don’t have full functionality on the watch, I should be able to switch to the phone quickly and easily and make whatever adjustment I need to, and then switch back to the watch. 

I used to start a routine on my watch and when I realized I needed to skip a task, I’d open up my phone and do it because I get to choose how to handle the skipped task as I’m skipping it. Then I’d just continue on the watch, no ending and restarting necessary. Now that the watch and phone app have been separated, I have to end the routine to make adjustments and that seems to be causing problems on top of being really inconvenient.

title: Load time and constant reminders already clicked on will make you ADD if you weren’t already
text:
Update 6-4-25: Every update downloaded just makes the app more prone to glitches, freezing and deletion of data. I’ve given the app many months and heard many promises of improvement from the developers. Unfortunately, the function just gets worse. If you have an older iPhone, don’t download this app. It’s poor and inconsistent performance will not ease ADD symptoms but make them worse. 

My original Routinery app review submitted 8-29-24: 
The app gets four stars mostly because of the size of the problem it is trying to solve. However, the biggest reason it gets four stars instead of fewer is that they’re really don’t seem to be any other options for people whose mind works the way mine does. The app is worth the annual fee charged no question. However, a handful of improvements could make it worth two or three times the price and simultaneously still be a five star value! number one decrease the battery usage, especially during longer tasks and with respect to notifications, for example I have an older model iPhone there are two apps on my iPhone that use up one percent of battery almost every minute that I am using that app: Google Maps is one and Routinery is the other. I can sort of understand why Google maps requires so much battery considering the sheer computational power of providing real time traffic information and navigation at such granular detail With street level video. On the other hand, why exactly does Routinery require so much battery? I think it must be a flaw in the design or some non-essential portion of the application that is not being regularly used by the customer are draining the customers device battery. Fix that and I’ll actually be able to use the routines that I created for Routinery currently I cannot— because within an hour and a half Routinery has drained a 100% battery. What about the other 17 hours of my working day I have routines set for those two and they aren’t things that can be run while my phone is plugged in just to conserve the battery required to use the app which reminds me what I’m supposed to be doing? I have very detailed twenty and thirty step routines over the course of two or three hours that I created— and mostly cannot even run on the app. Fix That and it’s a five star product. Improvement number two and this could just be nitpicky but the app for me glitches at least a half dozen times over the course of every day that I use— freezes the screen. I have to close the app and reopen it which takes half a minute sometimes. Actually a lot of times it takes me 30 seconds of trying to tap on the screen before I realize ‘oh it’s probably completely frozen and I need to shut it off and open it back up’. In a day we have 1440 minutes. I really dislike wasting five of them every day because of this smartphone glitch! it’s small annoyance but if you fix that and simultaneously double the price I would pay it and I suspect a lot of other people who are annoyed at the freezing Would happily do the same. Thirdly, there’s a setting somewhere in the apps software that is sending me a notification at 6 AM that says end of rest and another that says bedtime reminder at 11 PM. Neither of these is part of any of my routines that are currently activated. At least once per month I get so frustrated by this issue that I turn off all notifications for Routinery, just to stop those two notifications from waking me up when I am asleep. Please please make it easy to find inside the app where this can be turned off or tell me where it can be turned off if that setting already exists and my exhaustive search of the application has failed to find the setting!

title: Great app!!
text: This app is wonderful except it is a little hard to manage. It’s great and easy to use, but it makes you set a timer for everything, and though that is good to push your motivation, you don’t always know exactly what you’re going to do in that entire day and you can’t just pause it to continue later. You have to do it all in the time you have. What I did though is have a separate routine for my morning and evening, but you can do it however you’d like. It’s still really good and I recommend it if you’re having trouble actually getting things done or having a good routine or whatever you’re struggling with. This app even helped me to become closer to my religion, because I added a task for praying for 15 minutes in the morning and before I went to bed and it has helped so much. My life style is improving now even though this is only my first day using it. Though I said all those things earlier, I think you just have to get used to managing it, which it is pretty easy though. Again, it’s really good and I totally recommend it!! Love everyone reading this!❤️

title: absolute game changer
text:
This is one of the best apps i’ve ever used. I’ve tried so many routine apps, timers, but this one has been the most helpful so far. the constantly updating reminders of when the next task will start and when it will all end are IMMENSELY HELPFUL for actually keeping me on track/getting back on it after becoming distracted, which is generally my biggest routine struggle. The push notifications that can’t be dismissed are also absolutely crucial. The ability to rearrange tasks and choose to update only today or for all days is also pretty great. I also really enjoy the little in-app encouragements, I didn’t think much about them at first but they add up and are nice to see on bad days. I’ve spent money on premiums for apps before and have mostly been disappointed or frustrated after losing interest- i can honestly say that the paid version of this is absolutely worth it. Unlike most paywalled apps, the free version of this is perfectly good if you only have one or two routines. With no limit, my routines help me get ready for work, decompress at home, take my medication on time, and do my chores.

A feature I think I’d like to see one day would be the ability to add conditions to individual tasks (it only shows up on a Monday, it only shows up after a certain time of day, etc) in a single routine. This way, if my daily routine is the same every day but I have an extra chore to take care of on Mondays and another on Friday, I can have one daily routine that adapts. Currently you can do this by adding the task and simply skipping, but this makes the timers and “all ends” time slightly inaccurate.

Overall, this app has been life changing in taking some weight off my shoulders every day. I hope one day I can develop an app or tool like this that can benefit someone the way this app has benefitted me.

title: Mental Clarity
text:
I am the mother of a child with severe disabilities.  We have a lot of routine care tasks to track. Routinery has really helped me with mental clarity, and I feel much better since I started using it. i can’t say enough how helpful this app has been for me. 

I do have a wishlist. All of my routines are manual because I don’t start them at the same time each day. I wish there were a way to hide my usual evening tasks (like a bedtime routine) until later in the day because my entire list of daily routines has become too cluttered. I also wish there were seasonal, quarterly, semi-annual, and annual routine options. I also wish there were a way to make certain tasks show up only on certain days. For example, I water my houseplants on each Sunday, but I fertilize them once a month. It would be nice to be able to have it all as part of the same Sunday plant care routine with the fertilizer showing up only once per month.  I know I could duplicate the routine and set them for different Sundays, but any future changes to the routine would require the change to be made to each of those routines. I hope this makes sense.

UPDATE: I love this app, but I have so many routines that I am having difficulty finding and organizing them when I filter by activated routines. I wish there were some way to categorize the routines by day, frequency, and topic (like fitness, household, plants, etc. ) so I could pull them up to make any changes.

title: アップデート後にルーティンが全て消えた(復元確認済み)
text:
追記
丁寧なお返事をありがとうございます。
消えていたルーティンは復活しているのを確認しました(すでに新しく手打ちした方で運用を開始していたのでアーカイブにしました)
通知バグに関しては通知自体を許可しない設定に変更した為現在は問題ありません。
念の為、機種はiPhone 13 miniで iOS18.5です。
通知設定を10:15にして、その翌日から現象が発生しました。

信頼できる運営の方々だと判断して星を5に変更いたします。
YouTubeをバックグラウンドで聴いていて、音の邪魔をせずに遂行できるアプリが意外と少ないので助かっています。
いつもありがとうございます。

追記
通知のバグが発生しているのか、アプリを開くまで1秒おきに通知が連打して来ます。

追記
アカウント登録していなかったのでルーティンの復元はできませんでした。
アカウント登録ができると気づくのが遅かったようです。
幸い、週途中だったので履歴の中には詳細項目が書かれていた為、もう一度手打ちで全項目を入力していきます。

とても良いアプリで毎日使っていました。今回のタイマー変更のアップデートの案内後、私が作成していたルーティンが全て消えてしまいました。一つのルーティンに40項目位？登録していたので改めて手打ちしていくのは…。内容も完全には覚えていなくて困っています。
何か解決策はありますか？

title: 도미노 효과 + 체계적인 루틴 설계 및 빠르고 간단한 실행
text:
대략 삼 사 개월간 루틴 너리 앱을 써보고 난 뒤에 남기는 장점 입니다.
- 루틴이 끝나면 다음 루틴이 바로 시작 되기 때문에 내가 일 일이 타이머를 맞출 필요도 없고 연쇄적적으로 습관이 시작 되어서 원래 평소 라면 까먹거나 귀찮아서 잘 안했을 루틴들도 잘 챙기게 되는 효과가 있었습니다.
- 루틴별로 시간을 설정 해야 하기 때문에 타임 블로킹 효과가 있었습니다. 따라서 평소에는 막연하게 시간을 정해두 지도 않고 했었던 루틴을 정해진 시간 안에 의도적으로 할 수 있어 시간 활용을 더 효율적으로 할 수 있어 좋았습니다.

아쉬웠던 점도 있었습니다.
- 설정한 루틴을 시작하고 나면 이미 실행 중인 루틴의 이름을 수정 하는 것이 불가능 해서 살짝 불편했습니다. 예를 들어 평소에는 ’진로를 위한 시간갖기‘라는 제목에 루틴을 실행하는데, 어떤 날에는 ‘독서하기‘ 어떤 날에는 ‘글쓰기‘ 등으로 이름을 수정하여 실행하고 싶을 때가 있었습니다. 지금은 실행 중에 수정이 어려워서, 새로운 루틴을 생성 해서 추가한 뒤에 순서를 조정해야 하는 방식으로 하고 있습니다.

title: Super pour moi
text:
Très contente de cette appli de routine avec Timer. J’ai comparé avec plusieurs autres et c’est la plus pratique à utiliser dans le quotidien selon moi. 
J’apprécie vraiment les fonctionnalités accessibles avec un compte gratuit, c’est vraiment génial merci beaucoup !

- La possibilité d’enchaîner automatiquement ou manuellement les tâches est très pratique. 
- Pouvoir choisir le type de timer qui nous parle le plus est agréable à l’utilisation. 
- Je trouve aussi génial de pouvoir s’inspirer des routines de personnes connues notamment dans le développement personnel. 
- Je trouve juste dommage qu’une routine nocturne qui se termine après minuit soit automatiquement enregistrée sur le lendemain soir, du coup on doit restaurer la série ou perdre l’effet cumulé des routines ce qui est un peu frustrant.

En résumé ; application très pratique, agréable et intuitive que je recommande !

ですが1秒毎にアラームが鳴って鬱陶しいかったり小さな不具合が多いのでストレスを感じます。

アラームの方は適当な時間で鳴り止む機能がないので止めないとずーっとなり続けます。
一度だけ鳴るモードや数分だけ鳴るモードも増やしてほしいと感じます。
また小さなバグで言うと、スマートウォッチとの連携がうまくいかなかったり、アラームオフの表記がオンの表記になっていたりします。
コンセプト自体はとてもいいので改善を求めます。

できないことはパスしたり、ルーティンの最後に回したりしています。それでもこのアプリは「継続おめでとう」と褒めてくれます。

title: Helpful, but lacking
text:
This needs some feature updates for users who aren’t teenagers or young adults. More statistics—mood (not just mood on how do you feel about completing your routine), percentages of routine completed, correlation between mood and percentage of routine completed. 

This could be amazing if they focused less on incorporating things like the community aspect of the app and nonsense like celebrities’ routines and more on actual science and data. If, for example, users could see a positive correlation between completing at least 85% of their routines with an improvement in mood, many would certainly find routines—and this product—to be vital rather than something they downloaded on a whim and won’t renew next year. 

Developers need to consider they’re neglecting an entire pool of serious adult users who are also inclined to have deeper pockets than the teenage and college crowd do.

My therapist recommended an app like this, but my focus is to stay relaxed. The timer stresses me out so much. I can live with the timer, because I can just ignore it. title: Life changing Assistive tech
text:
I have been using this app for 3 months now, and it helped me to change my lifestyle entirely. 

I have pretty bad ADHD and this app is the best in making me do my regular drill without having to think about what comes next. Like, no mental load at all! I use it every day, for morning and evening routines. It is really so great because it also narrates the tasks and times, so I don’t need to be glued to the screen and can just get on with my business and it’s okay if my head is in the clouds. It also helps that ticking tasks is animated and each has an icon. Elements of gamification work wonders with my weird brain. I am still not bored with it after 3 months, because when I feel the routine getting old, I just change it!

Apart from making sure I locked the entrance door and switched off the gas every night, I also noticed that I spend much more time with things that matter to me as part of my routine. Tasks or times set apart for doing things that align with my values. It forced me to think about how I want to live life in general, and gave a shape to experiments with intentionality. I am seriously looking forward to starting every morning, because I will have little islands of peace and celebration programmed in, while also doing the essentials. The streaks also don’t break if I skip tasks sometimes so users are protected from the perfectionism trap while being able to celebrate getting through the routine anyway.
 
I am really grateful for the ad-free design (those would distract me a lot), but I also think the premium tier is affordable. I test a lot of habit management apps and this one is absolutely pro stuff, massive cheers to the developers and everyone that made it happen💚💚💚

title: Apple Watchとの連携が壊滅的
text:
アプリとしてはとても重宝していて、習慣化しやすい仕組みになっていると思います。

しかしながら、常にスマホを持ち歩いて行動するわけにはいかない習慣も多いため、Apple Watchで使用していますが、この連携が何年経っても杜撰です。

Apple Watchで習慣を起動していても、気づいたら勝手にアプリが終わっていたり、自動で次への設定になっているのに、いつまでも延長されたり。

ちなみに今日はルーティンが完了したのに、お疲れ様でした！と表示が出るだけでルーティン完了になっていませんでした。

結局スマホを開いてルーティンタスクのチェックマークを連打して完了扱いにするため、正確な所要時間も反映できません。

Apple Watchとの連携さえしっかりしてもらえたら完璧なアプリだと思います。

この1年課金して使用してきましたが、Apple Watchの連携問題が解決されるまでは課金はしないです。

それくらい酷い連携です。

title: 使いやすく重宝しているが…
text:
2025/09/30 
1日の終了時間を5:00amに設定しているにも関わらず、それが反映されていません。具体例を挙げると、夜のルーティンを月曜日の1:00amに開始して2:00amに終了した場合、設定が反映されていえば日曜日に完了したことになるはずですが、月曜日に完了したことになってしまいます。
私は帰宅時間が遅くなることがありその日のうちにルーティンを終えることができない日があるからこそ、日の境目を設定しているのに反映されていないため不便を感じています。せっかくの継続記録が途切れてしまうのはモチベーションの維持にも関わってきます。以前まではこのような不具合はなかったため、最近のアップデートが原因だと考えています。なるべく早い改善していただけると幸いです。

2025/10/19
丁寧なお返事ありがとうございます。現バージョンでは先日起こっていた問題が確認されていません。迅速な対応ありがとうございました。

title: This app keeps me sane (ADHD)
text: I really struggling to keep track of everything I needed to do to get ready in the mornings, and more than once have bcompletely forgot important tasks or objects before leaving for work. I also would often find myself standing in my kitchen trying to remember what else needed to be done, which was both exhausting and stressful. This app ended up being exactly what I needed. I've been using the app for about a year, and what is the most helpful to me is that it's essentially a list that resets itself everyday regardless of what I did or didn't do yesterday, no extra work needed on my part to reset it or fix it. It's also really nice that I can set an approximate amount of time for the task, so I have a better idea of how long I need to get it all done. This app ended up being so successful for what I needed that I started using it before bed as well. Now my laptop is always charged before I leave, the ice packs are frozen in the fridge, and I didn't forget to brush my teeth!

title: Very annoying to use
text:
The app is bloated with unnecessary features like social feeds and analytics. I wanted a straightforward habit tracker, not a lifestyle management tool. Its main function—creating habits with timed checklists—sounds good in theory, but in practice it’s rigid. I often multitask or switch the order of habits, which means constant reorganization. The timers create pressure instead of structure, and the voice prompts are intrusive.

The checklist system is the only redeeming feature, but even that lacks basic usability. There’s no quick “reset all” option, and notes for tasks are buried inside menus instead of being visible in the list view. 

The layout is poor. On iPhone it wastes space with oversized design elements, and on larger Android screens it looks cramped and unoptimized. Overall, the experience feels inefficient and overdesigned.

If you just want a clean, flexible daily routine tracker, avoid this one. Todoist and Apple Reminders are better, but Todoist can get cluttered and Reminders doesn’t sync well with Android. This app tries to do everything and ends up doing nothing well.

title: Top tier
text:
Amazing app. Incredibly helping for getting into routines.

I prefer this over individual habit tracking (which you can still do on here if you really want to), because:
1. You obviously get more done. 
2. Your brain is more likely to accomplish things when it’s at a set time each day
3. Your brain is more likely to accomplish things when you pair tasks together
4. A prompt is of the utmost importance for repeating desired behaviors. 

Set your goals small to start, just get into the routine, don’t overthink or overplan, and go from there.

title: The only truly helpful app for ADHDers
text:
You’re saving my life. I’d been literally falling apart till I found your app. Since then my life has changed hugely. I can’t say thank you enough : )


UPD: The app is super unreliable. When it works properly, it’s absolutely amazing.

But I’m freaking out when I need to do dances around a fire just to make it produce sound notifications!!!!
	1.	The app constantly asks for allowing notifications when I start a routine, but when you open the settings, there’s no such option there.
	2.	The app decides on its own whether to produce sound notifications. Some days it does, and some days it’s just “not in the mood.” And no matter what I do, it just doesn’t.

The whole point of this app is to tell me directly in my ear that it’s time to finish one thing and start the next, overcoming any other notifications or silent mode I have.

I wanted to add the app to the exclusions so I always receive notifications from it, but there is no such option for this particular app.

Whether sound notifications are produced or not doesn’t depend on the iPhone’s silent mode either. (Most of the time it works perfectly in silent mode, which I have on 99% of the time. But sometimes it doesn’t)

Sometimes I listen to an audiobook and the notifications go through to my headphones properly. Sometimes they don’t.

I would honestly switch to something more reliable, but I can’t find anything as convenient as this app. I don’t usually create routines - I create my entire next day in the app in the evening and then live my whole day with it. That was my way of beating procrastination: the app constantly tells me what I should do now and what I should do next.

So please, fix the notifications!

title: 이만한 앱이 없어요
text:
아이폰 사용자고, 유료 결제도 해서 정말 잘 쓰고 있어요. 다른 앱에 비해 직관적이고 심플하면서 있을 기능 다 있어서 정말 좋아요.
다만 몇가지만 개선해주시면 진짜 압도적인 앱이 될 것 같아요

1. 위젯 다양화
위젯이 좀 더 다양하면 좋겠어요 ㅠㅠ 지금은 위젯에서 루틴 한 가지만 월별 진행현황 확인할 수 있는데 한 위젯에서 여러 루틴 월별 현황을 확인할 수 있으면 좋겠어요. (ㅁㅇㄹㅌ 등 타사 앱 위젯 한 번 봐보시면 좋을 것 같아요)
잠금화면 위젯 추가됐으면 좋겠고, 아이폰 기준 가장 작은 사이즈 위젯이 앱 4개 들어가는 면적인데, 거기에 루틴 딱 하나만 표시되는 것도 아쉬워요. 루틴 4개 바로가기 만들려면 8칸 사이즈 위젯이어야 하는데 여기에 앱 몇개 같이 깔아놓으면 진짜 배경화면 안보이는 수준이거든요.

2. 디자인/커스텀 기능
별건 아닌데 폰트 다양화 가능했으면 좋겠어요. 어려우면 글자 사이즈라도요. 루틴을 한눈에 보고싶기도 한데 딱 앱 처음 들어가면 보이는 회색박스들 사이즈가 너무 커서 네개밖에 안보여요. 이 박스들 정사각형으로 만들어서 2열로 볼 수 있어도 좋을 것 같고, 사이즈를 좀 줄여주셔도 좋을 것 같아요. 그런 옵션을 주시면 설정에서 온오프로 컨트롤 할 수 있으니까 개인마다 자기 편한대로 할 수 있어서 좋을 것 같아요. 그리고 루틴 아이콘?도 좀 더 다양하게 생기면 좋을 것 같아요. 마음에 드는 걸 끝까지 못찾는 경우도 많아요. 좀 미감 신경쓴 그림체도 보고싶구 그림체별로 볼 수 있으면 좋겠어요.

3. 루틴 반복 설정 (매주)
루틴 반복 설정 옵션이 일간/주간/월간으로 있는네 전 그냥 매일 하고 싶어서 주간에서 요일 다 눌러놨거든요? 근데 시작화면에서 루틴하단에 ‘월화수목금토일’ 이렇게 뜨는 것도 아니고 ‘화수목금토일’ 이렇게 돼있는데 화수는 회색 채워진 동그라미, 금요일은 회색 안채워졌는데 테두리만 회색인 동그라미...
기준도 모르겠고 볼때마다 거슬려요. 루틴 진행현황인가요? 그건 다른 페이지에서도 볼 수 있으니 그냥 심플하게 주기만 ‘매일‘ ’화목’이런식으로  표시되면 좋겠어요.

4. 태그 상시표시
지금은 활성 탭을 누르고 오늘/활성/비활성 선택하고 태그 선택하고 확인까지 선택해야 활성화가 되는데, 그냥 위에 태그 다 띄워주시고 누르면 바로바로 그 태그에 해당하는 루틴만 떴으면 좋겠어요. 루티너리 앱을 사용하는 게 정돈된 삶을 살고 싶어하는 사람들인데, 이런 사소한 과정이 복잡스러우면 귀찮고 불편해요. 안그래도 루틴 많아서 유료결제하고 박스 커서 루틴 한 번에 다 못보는데 필터링 과정까지 복잡스러우니까 불편함이 은근 커요.

너무 길어졌는데 찐 애정 사용자 핃백이니까 한 번 내부에서 논의 부탁드려요ㅜㅜ 항상 잘 쓰고 있고 평생 쓰고싶어요

I go blind to random notifications but they cause so much mental clutter. I have kept this app because it helps improve my ADHD. The inability to turn these random tips off is driving me crazy, making me avoid the app prompts, and making me consider not renewing.

title: Game changer
text:
I don’t write a lot of reviews, but this app has been super helpful in keeping me on top of my daily routines so I feel compelled to write one now! It’s so much easier know to predict how long a routine task might take and to plan my day better, and it feels easier to focus on one task at a time when you know exactly how much time you’ve given yourself until the next task starts.

I do have some critiques, however. Firstly, the robotic text to speech voice is a little bit creepy and assertive. I’d be nice to have more naturalistic voice reminders if possible. Secondly, I’d find it helpful if there was a button to show the average task time since the first completion. The default length of a week is fine, but I’d like there to be an easier way to find the average across all completions than to have to reselect the dates on the calendar for every individual task.

All that being said, highly recommend for anyone looking to give themselves a bit more structure!
